item: the connecting-cleanup allocation sweep measures the waiting swap from the cleanup's start, with a 1.0 s window, and reports the figure (audit 0.5.0)
summary: test_a_memory_error_at_any_instruction_of_the_cleanup_leaves_no_level_raised_except_at_the_release_call failed once on CI with 'release_shared_since:209 CALL: a swap that was already waiting for the open did not get through' and passed on three other runs of the same interpreter. The library gets the waiting swap through in 0.05-0.11 s at that site (idle and beside 16 busy processes); the test timed it from the start of the swap's thread (it includes the body's own 0.05 s wait) against 0.5 s. A 0.7 s pause before the cleanup, with the library unchanged, reproduces the exact text on the old test and passes the new one. The time is now taken from the later of 'the cleanup began' and 'the swap asked', the window is 1.0 s inside a 3.0 s deadline (the no-step mutant still fails by name), the failure text carries the measured figure or 'refused at its deadline', and a swap that cannot get through because a level is left is not waited for (the file runs in about 5 s). What paused the CI process is not established. Test-only; src/database/library_generation.py is unchanged.
